description.value: The study investigated reward processing deficits and their anatomical correlates in behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia using pleasant, unpleasant, and neutral olfactory stimuli and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: Our objective was to identify the abnormal aspect of reward processing in bvFTD and identify its anatomical correlates.

value: We hypothesized that patients with bvFTD would respond less to negative olfactory stimuli than control subjects, and that this would relate to reward circuit atrophy, including the insula, which has been linked to processing of negative information (Seymour et al., 2007; Samanez-Larkin et al., 2008).

description.value: A series of olfactory tasks designed to evaluate reward consumption, reward anticipation, and effort to obtain reward or avoid punishment using pleasant, unpleasant, and neutral olfactory stimuli.

instructions.value: Participants smelled olfactory stimuli, rated their pleasantness, responded to descriptions of upcoming smells, and chose whether to smell or avoid each odorant.

stimuli.value: Pleasant olfactants: vanillin, menthol, and citral. Unpleasant olfactants: isovaleric acid, propionic acid, and pyridine. Neutral stimulus: propylene glycol.

value: Success at obtaining or avoiding selected stimuli
